concepts.title: Topographical Maps: Conventional Signs, Colours and Marginal Information
concepts.definition: Topographical maps drawn by the Survey of India on scales of 1:250,000, 1:50,000 and 1:25,000 show relief by contours and spot heights, and use conventional signs in colours of black for names, blue for water, brown for contours, green for vegetation, red and yellow for roads and settlements, with marginal information of sheet number, scale and administrative details.
concepts.textbook_ref: Reading the margin first tells the sheet number, scale, grid references and the administrative data of the mapped area.

concepts.title: Reading Relief: Contours, Slopes and Drainage on Topo Sheets
concepts.definition: Contours join points of equal height, and their spacing and pattern reveal concave, convex, uniform and terraced slopes, V-shaped contours crossing rivers, hills, plateaus, ridges, spurs, passes and valleys, so the physical and cultural landscape of the mapped region can be reconstructed from the sheet.
concepts.textbook_ref: Closely spaced contours mean steep slope, wide spacing means gentle slope, and evenly spaced contours mean uniform slope.

concepts.title: Interpretation of Human and Economic Features on Topo Sheets
concepts.definition: Beyond relief, topo sheets reveal settlement patterns of nucleated or dispersed villages, land use of cultivated and wasteland, transport routes, wells, tanks, temples and post offices, so the interpreter reconstructs the economy and life of the region from conventional signs.
concepts.key_idea: Green wash with field boundaries shows agriculture, blue tanks show irrigation, and lines of huts along roads show ribbon settlement.
